terms.grammar: first person of the old verb quaesō, thrown into the sentence; plural quaesumus
terms.comment: The polite “please” of prose as well as comedy (Cicero’s letters: quaesō).

terms.grammar: first person of obsecrō, often with tē
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 765b: Manē, manē, obsecrō tē.
terms.comment: Stronger than quaesō: “please, I beg you”. Plautus also spells it opsecrō.

evidence: Plaut. Most. 1: Exī ē culīnā sīs forās, mastīgia.

terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter., Hor.; Cic. in epistulīs
evidence: Ter. Ph. 103: Eāmus; dūc nōs, sōdēs.
Cic. Att. 7.3.11: jubē sōdēs nummōs cūrārī

phrases.english: “Help me with it, please, Dad!” he said
Hey, boy, tell me, would you…
Let’s go; lead the way, please.

phrases.latin: Exī ē culīnā sīs forās, mastīgia.
phrases.english: Out of the kitchen, please, you rascal.
Please, for goodness’ sake, get up; Father’s coming.

sources: Lewis & Short: amo
